sanskrit: ātmaprāṇaiḥ priyatamā bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ tvaṃ bhadre dharmataḥ pūjyā guruputrī sadā mama
english: You are dearer than life itself to the great-souled son of Bhṛgu; O noble one, you are by dharma always to be honoured by me as the daughter of my guru.

sanskrit: yathā mama gurur nityaṃ mānyaḥ śukraḥ pitā tava devayāni tathaiva tvaṃ naivaṃ māṃ vaktum arhasi
english: Just as Śukra, your father, is always my revered guru, so too are you, O Devayānī; therefore you ought not to speak to me in this way.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca guruputrasya putro vai na tu tvam asi me pituḥ tasmān mānyaś ca pūjyaś ca mamāpi tvaṃ dvijottama
english: Devayānī said: You are indeed the son of a guru's son, but you are not my father's son; therefore you too are honourable and worthy of reverence to me, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: asurair hanyamāne ca kaca tvayi punaḥ punaḥ tadā prabhṛti yā prītis tāṃ tvam eva smarasva me
english: When you were slain again and again by the asuras, O Kaca, recall for yourself the love I bore you from that time forward.

sanskrit: sauhārde cānurāge ca vettha me bhaktim uttamām na mām arhasi dharmajña tyaktuṃ bhaktām anāgasam
english: You know my supreme devotion in friendship and in love; you ought not, O knower of dharma, to abandon me who am devoted to you and guiltless.

sanskrit: kaca uvāca aniyojye niyoge māṃ niyunakṣi śubhavrate prasīda subhru tvaṃ mahyaṃ guror gurutarī śubhe
english: Kaca said: You are pressing me into a duty in a matter where I cannot be employed, O you of beautiful vows; be gracious, O fair-browed one — to me you are more revered than even my guru, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: yatroṣitaṃ viśālākṣi tvayā candranibhānane tatrāham uṣito bhadre kukṣau kāvyasya bhāmini
english: Where you dwelt, O wide-eyed one, O moon-faced one, there too did I dwell, O noble one — in the womb of Kāvya himself, O passionate one.

sanskrit: bhaginī dharmato me tvaṃ maivaṃ vocaḥ śubhānane sukham asmy uṣito bhadre na manyur vidyate mama
english: You are by dharma my sister; do not speak thus, O beautiful-faced one. I have dwelt at ease, O noble one; there is no anger in me.

sanskrit: āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi śivam āśaṃsa me pathi avirodhena dharmasya smartavyo 'smi kathāntare apramattotthitā nityam ārādhaya guruṃ mama
english: I take my leave of you and shall go; wish me good fortune on my path. I am to be remembered without violating dharma. Rise ever with diligence and worship my guru.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca yadi māṃ dharmakāmārthe pratyākhyāsyasi coditaḥ tataḥ kaca na te vidyā siddhim eṣā gamiṣyati
english: Devayānī said: If you, having been urged, reject me for the sake of dharma and desire, then, O Kaca, this knowledge of yours shall not reach fulfilment.

sanskrit: kaca uvāca guruputrīti kṛtvāhaṃ pratyācakṣe na doṣataḥ guruṇā cābhyanujñātaḥ kāmam evaṃ śapasva mām
english: Kaca said: I refuse because you are the guru's daughter, not because of any fault; and I have been released by my guru. Curse me thus if you wish.

sanskrit: ārṣaṃ dharmaṃ bruvāṇo 'haṃ devayāni yathā tvayā śapto nārho 'smi śāpasya kāmato 'dya na dharmataḥ
english: I speak the ancient law of the seers, O Devayānī; as you have cursed me, I do not deserve this curse — it comes from passion, not from dharma.

sanskrit: tasmād bhavatyā yaḥ kāmo na tathā sa bhaviṣyati ṛṣiputro na te kaś cij jātu pāṇiṃ grahīṣyati
english: Therefore the desire you have shall not be fulfilled thus; no son of a seer shall ever take your hand in marriage.

sanskrit: phaliṣyati na te vidyā yat tvaṃ mām āttha tat tathā adhyāpayiṣyāmi tu yaṃ tasya vidyā phaliṣyati
english: The knowledge shall not bear fruit for you — what you said of me shall be so likewise; but I shall teach another, and for him the knowledge shall bear fruit.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā dvijaśreṣṭho devayānīṃ kacas tadā tridaśeśālayaṃ śīghraṃ jagāma dvijasattamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to Devayānī, Kaca, best of twice-born, quickly departed to the abode of the lord of the thirty gods.

sanskrit: tam āgatam abhiprekṣya devā indrapurogamāḥ bṛhaspatiṃ sabhājyedaṃ kacam āhur mudānvitāḥ
english: Beholding him arrived, the gods with Indra at their head, rejoicing, honoured Bṛhaspati and then spoke these words to Kaca.

sanskrit: yat tvam asmaddhitaṃ karma cakartha paramādbhutam na te yaśaḥ praṇaśitā bhāgabhāṅ no bhaviṣyasi
english: The most wonderful deed you have done for our benefit — your glory shall never perish; you shall be a sharer of our offerings.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṛtavidye kace prāpte hṛṣṭarūpā divaukasaḥ kacād adhītya tāṃ vidyāṃ kṛtārthā bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Kaca had mastered his knowledge and returned, the gods, joyful in appearance, having studied that knowledge from Kaca, became fulfilled in their purpose, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: sarva eva samāgamya śatakratum athābruvan kālas te vikramasyādya jahi śatrūn puraṃdara
english: All of them assembled together and then spoke to Śatakratu: "Now is the time for your valour; slay your enemies, O Purandara."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sahitais tridaśair maghavāṃs tadā tathety uktvopacakrāma so 'paśyata vane striyaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the assembled thirty gods, Maghavan then said "So be it" and set forth; and he saw women in a forest.

sanskrit: krīḍantīnāṃ tu kanyānāṃ vane caitrarathopame vāyubhūtaḥ sa vastrāṇi sarvāṇy eva vyamiśrayat
english: Among the maidens who were playing in that forest resembling Caitraratha's garden, he, having become wind, mixed together all their garments.

sanskrit: tato jalāt samuttīrya kanyās tāḥ sahitās tadā vastrāṇi jagṛhus tāni yathāsannāny anekaśaḥ
english: Then those maidens, rising together from the water, seized those garments in many instances each as they came nearest to hand.

sanskrit: tatra vāso devayānyāḥ śarmiṣṭhā jagṛhe tadā vyatimiśram ajānantī duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: There Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, not knowing, took the mixed-up garment of Devayānī.

sanskrit: tatas tayor mithas tatra virodhaḥ samajāyata devayānyāś ca rājendra śarmiṣṭhāyāś ca tatkṛte
english: Then a quarrel arose between the two of them there, O king of kings, between Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā on account of it.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca kasmād gṛhṇāsi me vastraṃ śiṣyā bhūtvā mamāsuri samudācārahīnāyā na te śreyo bhaviṣyati
english: Devayānī said: Why do you take my garment, having become a pupil of mine, O demoness? It shall not go well with you, being devoid of proper conduct.

sanskrit: śarmiṣṭhovāca āsīnaṃ ca śayānaṃ ca pitā te pitaraṃ mama stauti vandati cābhīkṣṇaṃ nīcaiḥ sthitvā vinītavat
english: Śarmiṣṭhā said: Your father praises and salutes my father again and again, whether seated or reclining, standing humbly and submissively.

sanskrit: yācatas tvaṃ hi duhitā stuvataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ sutāhaṃ stūyamānasya dadato 'pratigṛhṇataḥ
english: You are the daughter of one who begs, praises, and receives; I am the daughter of one who is praised, who gives and does not receive.

sanskrit: anāyudhā sāyudhāyā riktā kṣubhyasi bhikṣuki lapsyase pratiyoddhāraṃ na hi tvāṃ gaṇayāmy aham
english: Unarmed against one who is armed, empty against one who is full, you stir up trouble, O beggar-girl; you shall find a match to fight you back — I do not count you at all.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca samucchrayaṃ devayānīṃ gatāṃ saktāṃ ca vāsasi śarmiṣṭhā prākṣipat kūpe tataḥ svapuram āvrajat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Śarmiṣṭhā threw Devayānī, who had grown haughty and was clinging to her garment, into a well, and then went home to her city.

sanskrit: hateyam iti vijñāya śarmiṣṭhā pāpaniścayā anavekṣya yayau veśma krodhavegaparāyaṇā
english: Thinking "She is dead," Śarmiṣṭhā of wicked resolve departed without looking back toward home, carried away by the force of her anger.

sanskrit: atha taṃ deśam abhyāgād yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ śrāntayugyaḥ śrāntahayo mṛgalipsuḥ pipāsitaḥ
english: Then Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, came to that place, his horses exhausted, his steeds wearied, thirsting, seeking game.

sanskrit: sa nāhuṣaḥ prekṣamāṇa udapānaṃ gatodakam dadarśa kanyāṃ tāṃ tatra dīptām agniśikhām iva
english: He, the son of Nahuṣa, looking about at that waterless well, saw that maiden there, blazing like a flame of fire.

sanskrit: tām apṛcchat sa dṛṣṭvaiva kanyām amaravarṇinīm sāntvayitvā nṛpaśreṣṭhaḥ sāmnā paramavalgunā
english: Having seen her, that best of kings, with most soothing and gracious words of comfort, questioned that maiden of divine complexion.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ tāmranakhī śyāmā sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalā dīrghaṃ dhyāyasi cātyarthaṃ kasmāc chvasiṣi cāturā
english: "Who are you, copper-nailed, dark-complexioned, with well-polished gem-set earrings? You meditate at great length and deeply — why do you sigh so distressed?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca patitāsy asmin kūpe vīruttṛṇāvṛte duhitā caiva kasya tvaṃ vada sarvaṃ sumadhyame
english: "And how have you fallen into this well overgrown with creepers and grass? Whose daughter are you? Tell me everything, O slender-waisted one."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca yo 'sau devair hatān daityān utthāpayati vidyayā tasya śukrasya kanyāhaṃ sa māṃ nūnaṃ na budhyate
english: Devayānī said: I am the daughter of that Śukra who revives with his knowledge the demons slain by the gods; he surely does not know of me now.

sanskrit: eṣa me dakṣiṇo rājan pāṇis tāmranakhāṅguliḥ samuddhara gṛhītvā māṃ kulīnas tvaṃ hi me mataḥ
english: This is my right hand, O king, with copper-hued nails on its fingers; take it and lift me up — you are deemed nobly-born in my estimation.

sanskrit: jānāmi hi tvāṃ saṃśāntaṃ vīryavantaṃ yaśasvinam tasmān māṃ patitām asmāt kūpād uddhartum arhasi
english: For I know you to be self-restrained, valiant, and illustrious; therefore you ought to raise me who have fallen from this well.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tām atha brāhmaṇīṃ strīṃ ca vijñāya nahuṣātmajaḥ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe pāṇāv ujjahāra tato 'vaṭāt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Recognising her then as a brahmin woman, the son of Nahuṣa took her by the right hand and lifted her up out of that pit.

sanskrit: uddhṛtya caināṃ tarasā tasmāt kūpān narādhipaḥ āmantrayitvā suśroṇīṃ yayātiḥ svapuraṃ yayau
english: Having quickly raised her from that well, the lord of men Yayāti took his leave of that fair-hipped one and went to his own city.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca tvaritaṃ ghūrṇike gaccha sarvam ācakṣva me pituḥ nedānīṃ hi pravekyāmi nagaraṃ vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: Devayānī said: Go quickly, O Ghūrṇikā, and tell my father everything; for I shall not enter the city of Vṛṣaparvan now.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tu vai tvaritaṃ gatvā ghūrṇikāsuramandiram dṛṣṭvā kāvyam uvācedaṃ saṃbhramāviṣṭacetanā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: She quickly went to the demon mansion, found Kāvya, and spoke these words to him, her mind agitated with alarm.

sanskrit: ācakṣe te mahāprājña devayānī vane hatā śarmiṣṭhayā mahābhāga duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ
english: "I report to you, O greatly wise one, O greatly fortunate one, that Devayānī has been struck down in the forest by Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan."

sanskrit: śrutvā duhitaraṃ kāvyas tatra śarmiṣṭhayā hatām tvarayā niryayau duḥkhān mārgamāṇaḥ sutāṃ vane
english: Having heard that his daughter had been struck down there by Śarmiṣṭhā, Kāvya went forth in haste, grieved, searching for his daughter in the forest.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duhitaraṃ kāvyo devayānīṃ tato vane bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya duḥkhito vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing his daughter Devayānī there in the forest, Kāvya embraced her with both arms and, sorrowing, spoke these words.

sanskrit: ātmadoṣair niyacchanti sarve duḥkhasukhe janāḥ manye duścaritaṃ te 'sti yasyeyaṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā
english: "All beings receive sorrow and happiness through their own faults; I think there must be some misdeed of yours for which this requital has come upon you."

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca niṣkṛtir me 'stu vā māstu śṛṇuṣvāvahito mama śarmiṣṭhayā yad uktāsmi duhitrā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ satyaṃ kilaitat sā prāha daityānām asi gāyanaḥ
english: Devayānī said: Whether there be a requital for me or not, hear me attentively — what was said to me by Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan: and truly she said it — 'You are a singer of the demons.'

sanskrit: evaṃ hi me kathayati śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī vacanaṃ tīkṣṇaparuṣaṃ krodharaktekṣaṇā bhṛśam
english: "Thus does Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, repeatedly speak sharp and harsh words to me, her eyes red with anger."

sanskrit: stuvato duhitā hi tvaṃ yācataḥ pratigṛhṇataḥ sutāhaṃ stūyamānasya dadato 'pratigṛhṇataḥ
english: "You are the daughter of one who praises, who begs and receives; I am the daughter of one who is praised, who gives and does not receive."

sanskrit: iti mām āha śarmiṣṭhā duhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ krodhasaṃraktanayanā darpapūrṇā punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Thus does Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, speak to me again and again, her eyes flushed red with anger, filled with arrogance."

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ stuvatas tāta duhitā pratigṛhṇataḥ prasādayiṣye śarmiṣṭhām ity uktā hi sakhī mayā
english: "If I am the daughter of one who praises and receives, then I shall placate Śarmiṣṭhā" — thus was spoken by a companion of mine to me.

sanskrit: śukra uvāca stuvato duhitā na tvaṃ bhadre na pratigṛhṇataḥ astotuḥ stūyamānasya duhitā devayāny asi
english: Śukra said: You are not the daughter of one who praises, O noble one, nor of one who receives; you, O Devayānī, are the daughter of one who does not praise but is praised.

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvaiva tad veda śakro rājā ca nāhuṣaḥ acintyaṃ brahma nirdvandvam aiśvaraṃ hi balaṃ mama
english: Vṛṣaparvan himself knows that, as does king Śakra and Nahuṣa's son; my power is the inconceivable, transcendent, lordly Brahman, beyond all duality.

sanskrit: śukra uvāca yaḥ pareṣāṃ naro nityam ativādāṃs titikṣati devayāni vijānīhi tena sarvam idaṃ jitam
english: Śukra said: The man who always endures the harsh words of others — know this, O Devayānī: by him all this world is conquered.

sanskrit: yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodhaṃ nigṛhṇāti hayaṃ yathā sa yantety ucyate sadbhir na yo raśmiṣu lambate
english: He who restrains surging anger like a horse — he is called a charioteer by the good, not he who merely hangs on the reins.

sanskrit: yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodham akrodhena nirasyati devayāni vijānīhi tena sarvam idaṃ jitam
english: He who repels surging anger with non-anger — know this, O Devayānī: by him all this world is conquered.

sanskrit: yaḥ samutpatitaṃ krodhaṃ kṣamayeha nirasyati yathoragas tvacaṃ jīrṇāṃ sa vai puruṣa ucyate
english: He who repels surging anger here with patience, as a serpent sheds its worn-out skin — he is truly called a man.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃdhārayate manyuṃ yo 'tivādāṃs titikṣati yaś ca tapto na tapati dṛḍhaṃ so 'rthasya bhājanam
english: He who restrains wrath, who endures harsh words, and who, though afflicted, does not afflict in return — he is truly a vessel worthy of prosperity.

sanskrit: yo yajed apariśrānto māsi māsi śataṃ samāḥ na krudhyed yaś ca sarvasya tayor akrodhano 'dhikaḥ
english: One who sacrifices tirelessly every month for a hundred years, and one who is angered at nothing — of these two, the one without anger is the greater.

sanskrit: yat kumārāḥ kumāryaś ca vairaṃ kuryur acetasaḥ na tat prājño 'nukurvīta vidus te na balābalam
english: What enmity mindless boys and girls may stir up — a wise person ought not to follow that course; they do not know the distinction between strength and weakness.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca vedāhaṃ tāta bālāpi dharmāṇāṃ yad ihāntaram akrodhe cātivāde ca veda cāpi balābalam
english: Devayānī said: I know, father, even though I am young, the distinction between the paths of dharma here; I also know the difference in strength and weakness in the matter of non-anger and harsh speech.

sanskrit: śiṣyasyāśiṣyavṛtter hi na kṣantavyaṃ bubhūṣatā tasmāt saṃkīrṇavṛtteṣu vāso mama na rocate
english: For one who wishes to flourish ought not to tolerate the ungurly conduct of a disciple. Therefore dwelling among those of mixed conduct does not please me.

sanskrit: pumāṃso ye hi nindanti vṛttenābhijanena ca na teṣu nivaset prājñaḥ śreyorthī pāpabuddhiṣu
english: Those men who censure by conduct and by birth — a wise person seeking the highest good ought not to dwell among such evil-minded ones.

sanskrit: ye tv enam abhijānanti vṛttenābhijanena ca teṣu sādhuṣu vastavyaṃ sa vāsaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate
english: But those who recognise one's worth by conduct and by birth — among such virtuous ones one ought to dwell; that dwelling is said to be the highest.

sanskrit: vāg duruktaṃ mahāghoraṃ duhitur vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ na hy ato duṣkarataraṃ manye lokeṣv api triṣu yaḥ sapatnaśriyaṃ dīptāṃ hīnaśrīḥ paryupāsate
english: The ill-spoken, most terrible speech of the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan — I consider nothing harder to bear in all three worlds for one who, of lesser fortune, must attend upon the blazing prosperity of a rival.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kāvyo bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ samanyur upagamya ha vṛṣaparvāṇam āsīnam ity uvācāvicārayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kāvya, best of the Bhṛgus, filled with anger, approached Vṛṣaparvan who was seated and spoke to him directly without deliberation.

sanskrit: nādharmaś carito rājan sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva putreṣu vā naptṛṣu vā na ced ātmani paśyati phalaty eva dhruvaṃ pāpaṃ gurubhuktam ivodare
english: "Unrighteous conduct does not bear fruit at once, O king, like a cow; but if one does not see it in one's own self, it ripens surely in one's sons or grandsons — evil, when swallowed, inevitably bears fruit, as if eaten by a pregnant woman in the womb."

sanskrit: yad aghātayathā vipraṃ kacam āṅgirasaṃ tadā apāpaśīlaṃ dharmajñaṃ śuśrūṣuṃ madgṛhe ratam
english: "When you caused the brahmin Kaca, the grandson of Aṅgiras, to be slain then — he who was of blameless character, a knower of dharma, devoted to service, content in my house —"

sanskrit: vadhād anarhatas tasya vadhāc ca duhitur mama vṛṣaparvan nibodhedaṃ tyakṣyāmi tvāṃ sabāndhavam sthātuṃ tvadviṣaye rājan na śakṣyāmi tvayā saha
english: "On account of the undeserved killing of him, and on account of the assault on my daughter too, hear this, O Vṛṣaparvan: I shall abandon you along with your kinsmen; I shall not be able to remain in your domain, O king, with you."

sanskrit: aho mām abhijānāsi daitya mithyāpralāpinam yathemam ātmano doṣaṃ na niyacchasy upekṣase
english: "Ah, do you regard me, O demon, as one who speaks falsely — that you neither restrain nor heed this fault of your own?"

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvovāca nādharmaṃ na mṛṣāvādaṃ tvayi jānāmi bhārgava tvayi dharmaś ca satyaṃ ca tat prasīdatu no bhavān
english: Vṛṣaparvan said: I do not recognise unrighteousness or false speech in you, O Bhārgava; in you dwell both dharma and truth. May you be gracious to us.

sanskrit: yady asmān apahāya tvam ito gacchasi bhārgava samudraṃ saṃpravekṣyāmo nānyad asti parāyaṇam
english: "If you abandon us, O Bhārgava, and go hence, we shall enter the ocean; there is no other refuge for us."

sanskrit: śukra uvāca samudraṃ praviśadhvaṃ vā diśo vā dravatāsurāḥ duhitur nāpriyaṃ soḍhuṃ śakto 'haṃ dayitā hi me
english: Śukra said: Enter the ocean or flee to the four directions, O asuras; I am not able to bear anything displeasing to my daughter, for she is beloved by me.

sanskrit: prasādyatāṃ devayānī jīvitaṃ hy atra me sthitam yogakṣemakaras te 'ham indrasyeva bṛhaspatiḥ
english: "Let Devayānī be propitiated; my very life depends on her; I am the guardian of your welfare and security as Bṛhaspati is to Indra."

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvovāca yat kiṃ cid asurendrāṇāṃ vidyate vasu bhārgava bhuvi hastigavāśvaṃ vā tasya tvaṃ mama ceśvaraḥ
english: Vṛṣaparvan said: Whatever wealth of the lords of the asuras exists on earth, O Bhārgava, whether elephants, cattle, or horses — of all that you are the master over mine.

sanskrit: śukra uvāca yat kiṃ cid asti draviṇaṃ daityendrāṇāṃ mahāsura tasyeśvaro 'smi yadi te devayānī prasādyatām
english: Śukra said: Whatever treasure of the lords of the daityas there is, O great asura, I am its master; yet let Devayānī be propitiated if it pleases you.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca yadi tvam īśvaras tāta rājño vittasya bhārgava nābhijānāmi tat te 'haṃ rājā tu vadatu svayam
english: Devayānī said: If you are the master of the king's wealth, O father, O Bhārgava, I do not acknowledge that for myself; let the king speak for himself.

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvovāca yaṃ kāmam abhikāmāsi devayāni śucismite tat te 'haṃ saṃpradāsyāmi yadi ced api durlabham
english: Vṛṣaparvan said: Whatever desire you desire, O Devayānī, O pure-smiling one, that I shall bestow upon you even if it be hard to obtain.

sanskrit: devayāny uvāca dāsīṃ kanyāsahasreṇa śarmiṣṭhām abhikāmaye anu māṃ tatra gacchet sā yatra dāsyati me pitā
english: Devayānī said: I desire Śarmiṣṭhā as my maidservant, together with a thousand maidens; let her attend upon me wherever my father shall give me away in marriage.

sanskrit: vṛṣaparvovāca uttiṣṭha he saṃgrahītri śarmiṣṭhāṃ śīghram ānaya yaṃ ca kāmayate kāmaṃ devayānī karotu tam
english: Vṛṣaparvan said: Rise, O attendant-woman, bring Śarmiṣṭhā quickly; and whatever desire Devayānī desires, let her fulfil it.
